newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Taiwan open to more Australian goods.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Taiwan open to more Australian goods.

text.p: Taiwan will open its market to 2,000 Australian-built cars in 1997 under a trade deal announced by the Australian government on Friday.

"Highlights of the package are the opening of the Taiwanese market to 2,000 Australian-built cars next year, a 40 percent cut in the discrimination faced by Australian beef, doubled quota access for Australian apples, and first-time access for stone and citrus fruits," Trade Minister Tim Fischer said in a statement.
The package was worth about A$30 million to Australian exporters, he said.

"We have been able to crack a number of long-standing market access problems, where Australian exporters have faced discriminatory import arrangements in Taiwan, particularly for beef and horticulture," Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said in a statement.
Import duties on beef would fall by 10 percent from early 1997, he said.
